---
title: broadcaster
---
## Check or Set if an Array is a Broadcaster {.unnumbered}


### Description

<code>broadcaster()</code> checks if an array is of class &quot;broadcaster&quot;. <br />
<code style="white-space: pre;">broadcaster()&lt;-</code> sets or un-sets the class attribute &quot;broadcaster&quot; on an array. <br />
<br />
The <code>broadcaster</code> class is a simple (or &quot;lazy&quot;) class,
and exists purely to overload the math, Boolean, and relational infix operators
to support broadcasting. <br />
This makes mathematical expressions with multiple variables,
where precedence may be important,
far more convenient. <br />
Like in the following calculation: <br />
<code>x / (y + z)</code> <br />
<br />

The <code>broadcaster</code> class comes with its own method dispatch for the base operators. <br />
If at least one of the 2 arguments of the base operators is of class <code>broadcaster</code>,
and no other class (like <code>bit64</code>) interferes,
broadcasting will occur in the same manner as used in the various <code style="white-space: pre;">bc.*</code> - functions. <br />
<br />



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>broadcaster(x)

broadcaster(x) &lt;- value
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="x">x</code></td>
<td>
object to check or set.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="value">value</code></td>
<td>
set to <code>TRUE</code> to make an array a broadcaster,
or <code>FALSE</code> to remove the broadcaster class attribute from an array.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

For <code>broadcaster()</code>: <br />
<code>TRUE</code> if an array or vector is a broadcaster, or <code>FALSE</code> if it is not. <br />
<br />
For <code style="white-space: pre;">broadcaster()&lt;-</code>: <br />
Returns nothing,
but sets (if right hand side is <code>TRUE</code>)
or removes (if right hand side is <code>FALSE</code>)
the &quot;broadcaster&quot; class attribute. <br /> <br />



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA}
library("broadcast")



x <- 1:10
broadcaster(x) <- TRUE

y <- 1:10
broadcaster(y) <- TRUE

x + y / x
x + 1 # mathematically equivalent to the above, since x == y
(x + y) / x
2 * x/x # mathematically equivalent to the above, since x == y

dim(x) <- c(10, 1)
dim(y) <- c(1, 10)

x + y / x
(x + y) / x

(x + y) * x




```
